idiom_name: java.util.Optional map/flatMap/filter + Stream.flatMap with explicit empty-stream conversion
implementation_notes: java.util.Optional is the 0..1 focus: map, flatMap and filter compose absent-aware steps without explicit isPresent checks. In Java 8 a stream of optionals has to be flattened by a mapper that returns Stream.of(value) or Stream.empty(), and that flatMap is the plural traversal; the classic optic structure is replaced by these two standard-library types. This is the widest-applicable realization and therefore the default; move to Optional.stream as soon as the floor is Java 9.
code_sketch:
Optional<String> city = Optional.ofNullable(order)
        .map(Order::customer).map(Customer::city);   // 0..1

List<String> cities = orders.stream()
        .map(Order::city)
        .flatMap(o -> o.isPresent() ? Stream.of(o.get()) : Stream.empty())
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
pitfalls: Optional is a value-based class: identity-sensitive operations (==, identity hash code, synchronization) have unpredictable results; compare with equals and test with isPresent/orElse.
Optional.get without a presence check reintroduces the failure the type removed; use orElse/orElseThrow, and avoid Optional in fields or hot paths where it allocates per access.

variants.name: Stream.mapMulti zero-or-one replacement (Java 16)
variants.implementation_notes: Java 16 adds mapMulti, which replaces each stream element with zero or more elements through a Consumer instead of allocating a Stream per element the way flatMap does; applied to an optional element it is Optional::ifPresent as a pipeline operator. Choose it over flatMap(o -> o.stream()) on Java 16+ when each element is replaced by a small (possibly zero) number of elements, the case the Javadoc names as preferable for mapMulti.
pitfalls: mapMulti mutates through the consumer: calling it more than once per element is legal but surprising, and calling it after the method returns is not.
